answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, slowly earned stake before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. A registry ties the stake to a rotating key, while a kernel checks that one stake cannot authorize concurrent identities; a cipher can protect private account links, and pigment can label reputation scores without exposing them. Splitting into Sybils then requires buying and locking more stake, which raises entry cost and forfeits capital during disputes or slashing.
